title: Polar Avenue Logistics outbound & pilot scratchpad
body:
Quick brain-dump for Polar Avenue Logistics (PAL) outreach and a lightweight pilot proposal. Notes to self — rough, actionable, not customer-facing unless cleaned up.

Background + why I care:
- PAL = regional last-mile + white-glove e-comm logistics (east coast warehouses, 400 drivers, 3rd-party carriers).
- Recent press: raised Series B (Aug 2024), hiring heavy on ops and SRE. High growth, pain around scaling driver support and customer chat volumes.
- Tech stack: Ruby/Go backend, Postgres, Kafka, in-house route planner (heuristic + ML). Mobile driver app (iOS/Android), web ops console. They run on AWS, some sensitive client contracts require VPC + audit logs.

Observed pains (from discovery notes + job posts + public S-1-esque deck):
- Support load spikes during peak windows (holidays). Response SLA targets missed at 15%+ on-night windows.
- Driver onboarding takes 2–3 hours due to manual forms and fragmented knowledge (route exceptions, client-specific rules).
- Their route suggestion model is costly to run and not always explainable — ops asks for clearer reasoning when rerouting.
- Security/compliance: enterprise retail clients ask for SOC2 + customer data isolation.

Why Redwood could matter (value props tailored):
- Predictable latency for driver-facing interactions (hosted or Private). Low tail latency matters for live reroute + ETA updates.
- Private deployment (VPC + audit logs) addresses compliance asks quickly — good sales lever.
- Dedicated capacity for consistent throughput during peak windows avoids cold starts that spike SLA misses.
- Embeddings + semantic search for driver knowledge base (fast retrieval of client rules, exception handling).
- Reranking for support replies to reduce average handle time + improve first-contact resolution.
- Cost controls: batching + cache suggestions could materially cut token costs for high-volume chat/notifications.

Hypothesis to test in pilot (small measurable bets):
1) Driver assistant prototype: on-device chat + quick KB retrieval reduces average driver help time from ~5min to <2.
   - Metric: time-to-resolution, number of escalations to ops.
2) Support auto-draft: generate support reply drafts for CS agents, aiming to reduce AHT by 20% and increase CSAT.
   - Metric: AHT, CSAT sample, % drafts used unchanged.
3) ETA clarity: use model to generate short human-readable reroute explanations for dispatchers to reduce rework.
   - Metric: dispatcher rework, manual overrides.

Pilot scope (4–6 week lightweight):
- Week 0: kickoff + access (VPC stub or demo data). Scope narrow: driver KB demo + 1 support channel.
- Week 1–2: ingest sample KB (10–20 client rule docs), set up embeddings store, connect quick UI (mocked mobile view).
- Week 3: run shadow drafting for support (no live send), collect metrics.
- Week 4: short live A/B for low-risk support queue (e.g., billing questions), measure AHT/CSAT delta.
- Deliverable: report + recommended configs (batching, caching, quantization) and cost estimate for full rollout.

Minimum requirements from PAL (ask during sales call):
- Access to representative support tickets (anonymized) + 20–30 driver KB docs/FAQs.
- A staging endpoint for driver app to surface drafts (or demo screenshots).
- Security checklist: will they require on-prem or is VPC good? Who is their security contact?

Outreach sequence (multi-touch, ~3 weeks):
1) Short email to Head of Ops (2–3 lines) + 1-pager PDF with pilot outline. Keep subject: "Pilot idea: reduce PAL driver help time by 40%"
2) LinkedIn note to Head of Product + Head of Ops: very short, mention mutual contact? (check internal comms first)
3) Follow-up with value props + specific metric ask ("can we share 20 anonymized tickets?")
4) If no response, send a curiosity email pointing at a specific example: "saw job req for Driver Ops — we built a driver KB for another carrier that cut escalations by 30%".

Draft outbound email (concise):
Subject: Pilot: cut driver help time and support cost at Polar Avenue
Hi {Name},
Saw PAL's growth and the hiring for Ops — congrats. We help logistics teams reduce driver help time and support AHT using small, private LLM deployments that sit behind your security controls.
Quick ask: would you be open to a 20–30 minute call to review a 4-week pilot that uses a small set of your KB + ticket data to prove impact?
If yes, I can send a one-pager + proposed timeline.
—Sofia

Longer email for product/tech lead (cadence step 2):
Hi {Name},
Wanted to share a brief pilot approach that maps to what I saw in PAL's public materials: fast experiments, clear metrics, and security-first deployment.
We'd run a 4–6 week scoped pilot focused on two wins: 1) driver-facing assistant for KB lookups (shadow mode -> live A/B), 2) support reply drafts for a single low-volume queue. Goal is to demonstrate measurable reductions in driver help time and agent AHT without touching production data (staging or anonymized samples).
Estimate: 2 engineers + 1 solutions lead, 4 weeks, pilot cost covered by Redwood for qualifying accounts.
If helpful, we can put together a short checklist for your security team.
Cheers,
Sofia Patel

LinkedIn touch (short):
Hey {Name}, quick note — Redwood does private LLM pilots for logistics teams. Have a 4-week blueprint that typically surfaces 20–40% reductions in internal handling times. Happy to share a one-pager if useful.

Objection handling cheat-sheet (concise responses):
- "We can't send customer data to third-party APIs": we can run in VPC or on-prem; provide KMS integration + full audit logs and can work on anonymized ticket exports.
- "LLMs are unpredictable / hallucinate": focus on retrieval-augmented generation for KB + rerankers; provide conservative templates and fallback to human review. Shadow mode for 2 weeks reduces risk.
- "Too expensive / unknown ROI": pilot is zero-cost for lead accounts; we instrument token usage and show exact $/ticket. Also batching/cache profiles reduce unit cost.
- "Integration time": start with export + offline embedding pipeline and a UI mock; prove value before integrating into mobile app.

Tech checklist for a quick engineering discovery call:
- Is there a staging cluster or can we get a nightly dump of anonymized tickets + KB? (format: JSONL CSV)
- Mobile app: are there screens where we can surface a short text snippet (e.g., canned tips) or do we need to prototype via web view?
- Auth: SSO? OAuth? Will we need service account or API key for staging?
- Security: SOC2? Any specific compliance artifacts they need from us?
- Traffic expectations for pilot: rough messages/day for driver help and support drafts.

Demo checklist (what to show in first call):
- 60s: What Redwood is (hosted, dedicated, private) with one-liner on latency + cost controls.
- 90s: Driver assistant flow (search KB -> suggested bullet answer -> confidence score).
- 60s: Support draft flow (ticket in -> draft reply -> edit/accept).
- 60s: Security slide (VPC, audit logs, KMS).
- 30s: Pilot ask + next steps (start w/ sample data, 4 weeks).

Internal asks / to-dos (Sofia):
- [ ] Check internal CRM for any existing PAL contacts (Salesforce).
- [ ] Sync with Solutions Engineering (Ethan) to prep a one-pager and a short demo build plan.
- [ ] Confirm budget for pilot credits with Growth Ops.
- [ ] Draft short security checklist to send to prospect's security team.
- [ ] Find any mutual connections on LinkedIn to warm intro.

Potential risks / unknowns:
- They might require on-prem rather than VPC — longer procurement cycle. Plan B: offer a data-minimized, staging-only pilot.
- Their route model vendor could see Redwood as a competitor — frame Redwood as augmentation (KB + support, not core routing initially).
- Need to confirm legal on anonymized ticket sharing (ask Legal for quick template).

Notes to self: keep messaging tight and metric-led. PAL will respond to clear ROI numbers (AHT, escalations, onboarding time). Avoid technical deep-dive until they ask; open with compliance + cost predictability.

Example quick KPI lines for email/one-pager (single-line bullets to use):
- Reduce driver help time by 30–50% in 4 weeks.
- Cut support AHT by ~20% with draft suggestions.
- Private VPC deployment + audit logs to meet enterprise retail contracts.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after first call.
